reasons.specificity: The reading precisely reconstructs the paper’s Horkheimer-to-Honneth contrast, anti-repair argument, eight-objection sequence, Finnish School occasion, and concluding concessions.
reasons.anchoring: Quoted phrases and cited sections occur in the paper and consistently support the attributed rhetorical operations, including the bounded distinction between rejecting monistic foundations and permitting selective borrowing.
reasons.non_obviousness: It usefully distinguishes the weaker refusal-to-concede inference from the stronger definitional argument and shows how chronology and concessions narrow the unsalvageability verdict.
reasons.coherence: The prose, appeals/framing table, reinforcement sequence, ledger, and counter-evidence maintain consistent attributions and preserve the distinction between textual invitation and actual reception.
reasons.usefulness: Both requested tables help readers trace how the paper establishes its standard, closes the repair option, accumulates objections, and qualifies its conclusion while explicitly leaving reception and motives unknown.
reasons.hallucination_risk: The analysis is highly cautious and source-bound, though its repeated claims of complete coverage and verification describe its own review process rather than something independently evidenced by the source.

score.one_line: An exceptionally well-anchored and useful rhetorical reading whose strongest contribution is narrowing the paper’s broad unsalvageability claim to its better-supported rejection of recognition as a unified foundation.
